queries.text: Harrison and Weiner (Human Biology, 1964), translated from the Portuguese edition quoted by the author; the English original is copyrighted, so this is a back-translation. “a tenção” in the source read as “a retenção” (retention).

translator_notes.text: Saci, caipora, curupira, and iara (spelled “yara” in the original) are mischievous or dangerous beings of Brazilian folklore (a one-legged trickster, forest guardians, a river siren). Kept as names; an English reader may need a note.
